FINRA Adopts Amendments to Rule 3220 (Influencing or Rewarding Employees of Others)
groups.summary: FINRA, as part of its FINRA Forward modernization initiative, has amended Rule 3220 (the Gifts Rule) effective March 30, 2026. The amendments raise the annual gift limit from $100 to $300 per recipient, codify and clarify prior interpretive guidance, and authorize exemptive relief. New supplementary material defines valuation and aggregation standards, clarifies supervision and recordkeeping obligations, and delineates categories of gifts that are excluded from the $300 cap and recordkeeping requirements: personal gifts for infrequent life events, bereavement gifts, de minimis and logo promotional items, commemorative items commemorating a business transaction (even if over $300), and certain disaster-relief donations. The rule is confirmed not to apply to gifts to a member’s own associated persons or to individual retail customers. FINRA also adopts conforming $300 gift limits in Rules 2310, 2320, 2341, and 5110, aiming to modernize the regulatory framework while maintaining investor protection and providing flexible, risk-based supervisory expectations.

groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to the Capital Acquisition Broker Rules
groups.summary: FINRA, as part of its FINRA Forward initiative, has adopted amendments to the Capital Acquisition Broker (CAB) rules, effective March 25, 2026, to reduce regulatory burdens on CABs while preserving their limited institutional business model and investor protections. groups.title: Reducing Burdens and Providing Guidance on the Use of Negative Consent for the Bulk Transfer or Assignment of Customers’ Accounts
groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-03 provides consolidated guidance and effective practices for broker-dealer members using negative consent to effect bulk transfers or assignments of customer accounts, while eliminating FINRA staff’s prior practice of pre-reviewing negative consent letters. The Notice reiterates that affirmative customer consent is generally required to transfer or assign accounts and that negative consent is appropriate only in limited bulk transfer circumstances driven by operational or business changes, where it can enhance efficiency and minimize account disruption. Effective April 1, 2026, firms no longer need to submit draft negative consent letters to FINRA for a "no objection" review, though FINRA will continue to offer interpretive guidance and review practices through examinations. The Notice outlines situations where negative consent has been used (e.g., firms leaving or changing lines of business, clearing or introducing firm changes, mergers, terminations of networking or plan arrangements, and certain directly held account scenarios). groups.summary: FINRA requests public comment on proposed revisions to its senior investor protection and anti-fraud rules. groups.title: Final Statements Now Available for Broker-Dealers, Investment Adviser Firms, Agents and Investment Adviser Representatives, and Branches
groups.summary: FINRA announces that Final Statements for the 2026 annual Renewal Program are now available in E-Bill for broker-dealers, investment adviser firms, agents, investment adviser representatives, and branches. These statements reflect final renewal fees as of December 31, 2025, incorporating changes since the Preliminary Statements. Firms that owe more than originally estimated must pay the additional fees by January 23, 2026, and must also report any discrepancies in writing by that date, including a descriptive letter, a copy of the Final Statement, and supporting documentation, mailed to FINRA’s Registration & Disclosure unit in Rockville, MD. Firms with credit balances from overpayments have had those credits moved to Flex-Funding Accounts as of January 2, 2026, and may request refunds through E-Bill or leave funds for future use; refund processing resumes January 26, 2026. FINRA emphasizes use of electronic payments via E-Bill, but also permits payment by wire or check, with detailed instructions available on the Renewal Program Payment Options page. groups.title: FINRA Amends Annual Reports Extension of Time Request Policy
groups.summary: FINRA has amended its Annual Reports Extension of Time Request Policy, effective December 29, 2025, to update the information required from firms and their auditors when requesting extensions to file annual reports under SEA Rule 17a-5(d) and (m)(1). The revised policy removes the prior requirement that the auditor represent that an unqualified audit opinion will be issued and shifts primary responsibility for certain regulatory compliance representations to the firm's Principal Financial Officer (PFO). Auditors must still provide a letter, but it is now limited to representations based on work completed as of the extension request date, including agreement or disagreement with the firm's representations and whether any issues may delay or prevent issuance of the auditor's reports. FINRA is phasing in the new policy for 2025 annual reports, allowing firms to choose either the new or previous policy during this interim period, and is rescinding the related, now-outdated interpretation to SEA Rule 17a-5(m)(1) in the Interpretations of the SEC’s Financial and Operational Rules.

groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to the Arbitration Codes to Accelerate the Processing of Arbitration Proceedings for Parties Who Qualify Based on Their Age or Health Condition
groups.summary: FINRA has adopted amendments to its Codes of Arbitration Procedure adding new Rules 12808 and 13808 to create an accelerated processing track for arbitration cases involving parties who qualify based on age or health. Effective for arbitrations filed on or after March 30, 2026, eligible parties can request accelerated processing at the time of filing a claim or answer if they are at least 70 years old or certify that a medical diagnosis and prognosis create a reasonable belief that faster processing is necessary to avoid prejudice. The Director of Dispute Resolution Services (DRS) will determine eligibility based on objective criteria without assessing the reasonableness of the party’s belief. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Rule 6730 (Transaction Reporting) to Streamline Allocation Reporting for BD/IAs
groups.summary: FINRA has amended TRACE transaction reporting Rule 6730 to allow firms that operate as both broker-dealers and investment advisers (BD/IAs) to report certain allocation trades to managed customer accounts on an aggregated basis rather than submitting separate TRACE reports for each individual account allocation. New Supplementary Material .08 permits a BD/IA, at its option, to file a single aggregate TRACE report covering multiple allocations of an aggregate order in a TRACE-eligible security to managed customer accounts, provided the allocations share the same price and time of execution, and the report is submitted within existing TRACE timeframes. The aggregate report must include the number of managed customer accounts receiving allocations, and FINRA will disseminate both the number of accounts and the aggregate allocated volume (subject to existing size caps). groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to the Arbitration Codes to Make Clarifying, Technical and Procedural Changes to the Arbitrator List Selection Process
groups.summary: FINRA amended its Codes of Arbitration Procedure to adjust how arbitrator lists are generated and managed, clarify existing practices, and tighten procedural timeframes. In three-arbitrator customer and certain industry cases, non–chair-qualified public arbitrators will now have two chances for selection on the public arbitrator roster by being included twice in the pool used to generate Public Lists, correcting an imbalance that favored chair-qualified public arbitrators. The amendments shorten from 30 to 20 days the time for the Director to send arbitrator lists after the last answer is due; codify the use of full employment histories and "disclosure reports" for arbitrator background information; formalize the process for anonymous party requests for additional arbitrator information, including a 10-day objection period and 5-day withdrawal window before requests are forwarded to arbitrators. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Extend the Trade Reporting Facilities Operating Hours
groups.summary: FINRA has amended Rules 6380A and 6380B to extend the operating hours of its Trade Reporting Facilities (TRFs) from 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. ET to 4:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m. ET each business day, effective March 30, 2026. OTC trades in NMS stocks executed between 4:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. ET on a business day must be reported as soon as practicable but no later than 10 seconds after execution, with specific modifiers for trades outside normal market hours. Trades executed when the TRFs are closed must be reported by 4:15 a.m. after the system opens, with required "outside normal market hours" and, where applicable, "as/of" designations. FINRA notes that the SEC received comments on the rule filing and that FINRA is still considering whether further action is needed. Technical specifications updates will be announced in future Technical Notices.

groups.title: Broker-Dealer, Investment Adviser Firm, Agent and Investment Adviser Representative, and Branch Renewals for 2026
groups.summary: FINRA's 2026 Renewal Program notice outlines processes, deadlines, and fee structures for the annual renewal of broker-dealer and investment adviser firm, agent, investment adviser representative, and branch registrations processed through CRD and IARD. The program relies on a Preliminary Statement, available November 10, 2025, showing initial renewal fees, and a Final Statement, available January 2, 2026, that reconciles fees based on registration status as of December 31, 2025. Beginning with the 2026 cycle, FINRA is implementing a tiered Annual System Processing fee based on the number of securities regulators per individual (excluding IA representative registrations), and modifying the existing tiered Annual Branch Renewal Registration fees, as previously announced in SR-FINRA-2024-019. Firms must pay the full amount of the Preliminary Statement by December 8, 2025; late payment can trigger late fees and potential business ineligibility in certain jurisdictions. groups.title: FINRA Enhances Its Systems to Facilitate Member Compliance With Form U4 Recordkeeping Requirements
groups.summary: FINRA announces that, effective October 10, 2025, member firms may rely on the Central Registration Depository (CRD) to satisfy recordkeeping obligations for Form U4 filings that are electronically signed via FINRA's Financial Professional Gateway (FinPro Gateway) using FINRA E‑Signature. This builds on SEC staff no‑action relief and extends prior permission that allowed reliance on CRD for certain unsigned uniform registration forms. Under FINRA Rule 1010(c) and Exchange Act Section 17(a) and Rule 17a‑4, members are required to base initial and transfer Form U4 filings, and certain amendments, on signed copies or written acknowledgments and to retain those records. The new no‑action relief permits firms that opt to use FINRA E‑Signature to treat CRD as the system of record for those signed Form U4s, potentially reducing firms' own record retention costs and administrative burden. Use of FINRA E‑Signature remains optional and free, and FINRA outlines procedural steps for firms to submit Form U4s through FinPro, including ensuring individuals have FinPro accounts, routing the form for review and e‑signature, and completing the firm representative signature before submission. groups.title: FINRA Announces Update of the Interpretations of Financial and Operational Rules
groups.summary: FINRA has updated its Interpretations of Financial and Operational Rules to incorporate several new SEC staff interpretations relating to Securities Exchange Act Rules 15c3-1 (net capital) and 15c3-3 (customer protection). The new interpretations address the net capital treatment of certain non-convertible and convertible debt securities and preferred stock with a ready market but elevated or unassessed credit risk, securities owed as compensation to registered persons that are non-transferable or restricted from sale, and open contractual commitment charges in competitive sales. A new interpretation also clarifies the treatment of free credit balances in customers' IRA accounts under Rule 15c3-3. In parallel, as part of the FINRA Forward initiative, FINRA has enhanced the online Interpretations by adding direct hyperlinks to referenced source materials (e.g., SEC staff no-action letters, FINRA notices, NYSE memos), aiming to simplify firms' access to underlying guidance and support their regulatory compliance.

groups.title: FINRA Reminds Members and Associated Persons, Wherever Located, of Their Obligation to Comply With Rule 8210
groups.summary: FINRA reminds member firms and associated persons that they must fully comply with FINRA Rule 8210 information and testimony requests regardless of where they or their books and records are located, including outside the United States. Rule 8210 authorizes FINRA staff and adjudicators to obtain information, testimony, and to inspect and copy books and records for investigations, complaints, examinations, and proceedings. Because FINRA lacks subpoena power, compliance with Rule 8210 is critical to its self-regulatory function, and failure to provide complete and truthful responses can result in severe sanctions, including expulsion or bars. The Notice emphasizes that there is no exception for conflicts with foreign laws that restrict responses to overseas regulators. Firms with foreign operations must design supervisory systems under Rule 3110 to ensure the ability to provide information, testimony, and records (including those held by third parties or abroad) and to ensure associated persons can appear for testimony at locations specified by FINRA, such as U.S. offices. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Require Use of a Portal in Proceedings Before the Office of Hearing Officers
groups.summary: FINRA has adopted rule amendments that mandate use of a new secure web-based OHO Docket Portal as the primary method for filing and service of documents in proceedings before the Office of Hearing Officers, replacing email and paper processes except in limited circumstances. Parties and their representatives must use the portal to submit and serve documents, and must provide an email address when appearing before OHO to enable portal registration. Reasonable accommodations and alternative methods of filing or service may be ordered for parties who cannot use the portal, and complaints and default-case papers will continue to be served only by personal service, mail, or courier. The changes are intended to improve efficiency, centralize access to case documents and deadlines, and preserve fair process, and they become effective October 7, 2025.

groups.title: FINRA Enhances Its Systems to Enable Members to Provide Associated Persons With Uniform Registration Form and Predispute Arbitration Information Through FinPro Gateway
groups.summary: FINRA is enhancing its Financial Professional Gateway (FinPro Gateway) to let member firms, on an optional basis, satisfy certain existing delivery requirements electronically starting November 3, 2025. Members may use FinPro Gateway to deliver Form U4 (including amendments), Form U5 (including amendments), and required predispute arbitration disclosures to associated persons under FINRA Rule 1010(c), Article V, Section 3 of the FINRA By-Laws, and FINRA Rule 2263. The enhancements are part of the FINRA Forward initiative to modernize compliance processes and reduce manual, paper-based delivery (e.g., via mail or third-party services). To rely on FinPro Gateway for these purposes, specific conditions must be met, including creation of a FinPro account by the associated person, member validation of email addresses, written notice from the member that it will use FinPro Gateway for these deliveries, acknowledgement by the associated person that they may receive required information through FinPro, and the member’s election in the system to use this delivery method. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Exemption From FINRA Rules 5130 and 5131 for Business Development Companies
groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 25-08 announces amendments to FINRA Rules 5130 and 5131 to create a new general exemption for business development companies (BDCs). Non-traded and private BDCs, defined by Section 2(a)(48) of the Investment Company Act, are exempted from Rule 5130 and the spinning provisions in Rule 5131(b), provided they are not formed or maintained for the specific purpose of allowing restricted persons to invest in new issues. Traded BDCs remain covered by the existing general exemption for publicly traded entities. The amendments aim to align the treatment of non-traded and private BDCs with registered investment companies and traded BDCs, enabling BDCs to access IPO allocations more easily while maintaining protections around the integrity of the public offering process. The effective date of the amendments is July 23, 2025.

groups.title: FINRA Requests Comment on Modernizing FINRA Rules, Guidance, and Processes for the Organization and Operation of Member Workplaces
groups.summary: FINRA’s Regulatory Notice 25-07 solicits public comment on a broad modernization of its rules, guidance, and processes as they relate to how member broker-dealers organize and operate their workplaces in an increasingly digital, decentralized, and technology‑driven environment. The notice emphasizes aligning regulation with modern business practices—such as hybrid and remote work, cloud services, AI (including generative AI), mobile access, and electronic communications—while maintaining investor protection and market integrity. groups.title: FINRA Requests Comment on Modernizing FINRA Rules, Guidance and Processes to Facilitate Capital Formation
groups.summary: FINRA’s Regulatory Notice 25-06 initiates a broad request for public comment on modernizing FINRA rules, guidance, operations, and administrative processes that affect capital formation. FINRA frames efficient capital raising as critical to economic growth and emphasizes its role, as an SRO, in continuously updating its regulatory framework to reduce unnecessary costs and burdens while maintaining investor and issuer protection. groups.title: FINRA Requests Comment on a Proposal to Reduce Unnecessary Burdens and Simplify Requirements Regarding Associated Persons’ Outside Activities
groups.summary: FINRA proposes a new, consolidated rule to govern the outside activities of associated persons by replacing FINRA Rules 3270 (Outside Business Activities) and 3280 (Private Securities Transactions) with a single framework focused on investment-related activities. The proposal narrows required reporting to higher-risk investment-related outside activities and outside securities transactions, preserving core investor protections while reducing compliance burdens from low-risk, non-investment-related work. Registered persons must continue to provide prior written notice of outside activities, and associated persons must provide prior written notice of outside securities transactions, with differing member obligations depending on whether selling compensation is involved. The rule introduces a standardized assessment process, clarifies treatment of portfolio managers and investment committee members, codifies allocation agreements where a person is associated with multiple members, and provides several exclusions (e.g., activities for affiliates, family transactions without selling compensation, Rule 3210 accounts, and personal non-securities investments). groups.title: FINRA Launches Broad Review to Modernize Rules Regarding Member Firms and Associated Persons
groups.summary: FINRA issues Regulatory Notice 25-04 announcing a broad, multi-year initiative to modernize its rules governing member firms and associated persons. The initiative aims to enhance investor protection and market integrity by updating requirements to reflect current and emerging market practices, technology, and overlapping non-FINRA regulatory frameworks. FINRA identifies two initial focus areas—capital formation and the modern workplace—on which it will issue targeted requests for comment. The Notice solicits public comment by May 12, 2025 on specific rules, rule groupings, guidance, reporting and data requirements, and areas where FINRA’s oversight may duplicate or conflict with other regulatory regimes. FINRA frames this effort as an expansion of its retrospective review program and emphasizes its intent to remove unnecessary burdens, support innovation and new technologies, and better align broker-dealer oversight with today’s business models and regulatory environment.

groups.title: 2025 GASB Accounting Support Fee to Fund the Governmental Accounting Standards Board
groups.summary: FINRA announces the 2025 Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Accounting Support Fee, which FINRA is required to assess and collect under Section 14 of Schedule A to its By-Laws and an SEC order under Section 19(g) of the Securities Act of 1933. For 2025, GASB's total budgeted expenses are $18,897,700, partially offset by $1,599,600 of excess reserves from the Financial Accounting Foundation (FAF), resulting in $17,298,100 of recoverable annual budgeted expenses to be funded through the fee. FINRA will therefore assess and collect $4,324,525 per calendar quarter beginning in April 2025 from member firms that report municipal securities transactions to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB). groups.title: Guidance to Members Affected by California Wildfires
groups.summary: FINRA issues temporary regulatory relief and operational guidance for member firms and associated persons affected by the January 2025 California wildfires. The Notice addresses emergency office relocations and expanded remote-work arrangements, suspension of certain Form U4 and Form BR location-update requirements, flexibility on branch inspections, and accommodations for delayed regulatory filings, responses to inquiries, and customer margin collection. FINRA will delay specified assessments and waive related late fees, and plans to seek waivers of certain late trade reporting fees. Firms are encouraged to update customer communications, including website notices about account access, and are reminded of conditions for holding customer mail under Rule 3150, with instructions to contact FINRA when customers cannot be reached for consent or check-delivery alternatives. The Notice clarifies that disaster-related donations to affected institutional customers’ employees are not treated as prohibited gifts under Rule 3220(a). groups.title: Broker-Dealer and Investment Adviser Renewals for 2025
groups.summary: FINRA Notice 25-01 outlines the 2025 annual renewal process for broker-dealer and investment adviser registrations, exempt reporting, and notice filings handled through CRD and IARD. Final Statements, reflecting firms’ status as of December 31, 2024, are available in E-Bill as of January 2, 2025, incorporating adjustments since Preliminary Statements. If Final Statements show higher fees than previously assessed, additional renewal fees must be paid by January 24, 2025, which is also the deadline to report any discrepancies in writing with supporting documentation. Overpayments have been credited to firms’ Flex-Funding Accounts, and refund processing will resume January 27, 2025. FINRA recommends firms use E-Bill for payments, verify that their Renewal Statement balances are paid in full, set up email notifications, and carefully review renewal reports in CRD/IARD for accuracy, keeping these reports as part of their permanent records. Contact information is provided for both general support and discrepancy-related questions, and FINRA notes that, in the case of any misunderstanding, the underlying rule language controls over the explanatory notice.

groups.title: Unexpected Close of Securities Markets
groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 24-18 provides updated guidance for broker-dealer members on how to treat an unexpected close of U.S. securities markets ("the day of closure") for purposes of key financial responsibility, margin, reporting, and close-out rules. Based on discussions with SEC and Federal Reserve staff, the Notice clarifies when the day of closure should be treated as a regular business day versus a non-business day under SEA Rules 15c3-1, 15c3-3, 17a-5, Rule 204 under Regulation SHO, FINRA Rules 4210, 4230(b), 4521, 4524, and Federal Reserve Board Regulation T. In general, the day of closure is treated as a business day for net capital aging, customer protection possession or control, margin calls, day-trading equity lock-up, and certain extension-of-time calculations, but may be treated as a non-business (or non-calendar) day for some financial and regulatory reporting deadlines and for Regulation SHO Rule 204 close-out timing when equity markets are closed. groups.title: FINRA Requests Comment on Proposed Changes to Corporate Financing Rules
groups.summary: FINRA is requesting public comment on proposed amendments to Rules 5110 (Corporate Financing), 5121 (Conflicts of Interest in Public Offerings), and 5123 (Private Placements). groups.title: Amendments Relating to the Applicability of the Document Production Lists to Simplified Customer Arbitrations Administered Under Rule 12800
groups.summary: FINRA is amending its Customer Code to clarify and partially expand how the Discovery Guide's Document Production Lists apply in simplified customer arbitrations under Rule 12800, effective for cases filed on or after March 3, 2025. Previously, the Lists applied only when a customer chose a regular (Option One) hearing and did not apply to paper cases or Option Two special proceedings. Under the amendments, customers in paper cases and special proceedings may affirmatively elect to have the Document Production Lists apply to all parties by making a timely request when filing the claim (Rule 12302) or, for customer-respondents, by the Rule 12303 answer due date. If the customer does not timely elect, the Document Production Lists will not apply by default, but arbitrators retain discretion to use relevant portions in a manner consistent with the expedited nature of simplified proceedings, and parties may still request discovery directly from each other. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to the Codes of Arbitration Procedure to Provide Customers With a Copy of the Official Record of an Expungement Hearing
groups.summary: FINRA has amended Rules 12606 and 13606 of the Codes of Arbitration Procedure, effective for arbitration cases filed on or after December 1, 2024, to (1) require the Director of FINRA Dispute Resolution Services to provide, upon request, a copy of the official record of an expungement hearing under Rule 13805 (and any transcription) to customers who either attend and participate in the expungement hearing or submit a written position on the expungement request, and (2) update references to hearing recordings to reflect current practice of using digital or other recordings instead of tape. These changes complement earlier amendments to the expungement process for customer dispute information by ensuring customers have access not only to documents filed in a straight-in expungement request, but also to the official hearing record.

groups.title: Broker-Dealer, Investment Adviser Firm, Agent and Investment Adviser Representative, and Branch Renewals for 2025
groups.summary: This FINRA Regulatory Notice describes the 2025 Renewal Program for broker-dealer and investment adviser firms, their agents/representatives, and branches. It explains how renewal fees for registrations and notice filings through CRD and IARD are calculated, communicated, and collected, and emphasizes key operational deadlines. Preliminary Statements of renewal fees will be available in E‑Bill starting November 11, 2024, and must be fully paid by December 9, 2024, to avoid late fees for FINRA-registered firms. groups.title: FINRA Requests Comment on the Effectiveness and Efficiency of its Requirements Relating to Day Trading
groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 24-13 announces a retrospective review of its rules governing day trading, seeking public comment on whether the existing framework remains effective and efficient given major changes in markets, technology, and investor behavior since the rules were adopted in 2000–2001. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Rule 3240
groups.summary: FINRA has adopted amendments to Rule 3240 governing borrowing and lending arrangements between registered persons and their customers, effective April 28, 2025. The amendments strengthen the general prohibition by clarifying its application to pre-existing arrangements, expanding the definition of "customer" to include any customer who has or in the prior six months had an account assigned to the registered person at any member, and extending the rule to arrangements involving similar conflicts, including owner-financing. groups.summary: FINRA has updated its longstanding set of interpretations under FINRA Rule 4210 (Margin Requirements). The revised interpretations are effective immediately upon publication of Regulatory Notice 24-11 and are available on the FINRA website under "Interpretations of Rule 4210." The prior interpretations, dated October 27, 2021, are being retired but will remain accessible online for reference. FINRA has also published a guide that compares the new interpretations with the 2021 version and provides additional information on the updates, along with other margin-related reference materials on its Margin Regulation webpage.

groups.title: FINRA Reminds Members of its Policy Prohibiting Members From Recording FINRA Calls and Meetings
groups.summary: FINRA reaffirms and updates its longstanding policy that member firms and their associated persons are prohibited from making audio or video recordings of conversations, calls, or meetings with FINRA staff conducted in connection with examinations, investigations, or any other oversight functions, including through automated recording or AI/virtual meeting tools. FINRA cites concerns about potential editing or alteration of recordings, inaccuracies in AI-generated transcripts or summaries, and consistency with FINRA Rule 2010 and certain state consent-to-recording laws. Members should not expect FINRA to consent to recording, which will only be allowed in rare circumstances. FINRA also states that, as a general matter, its own staff will not record such interactions without consent from the parties.

groups.title: FINRA Reminds Members of Regulatory Obligations When Using Generative Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models
groups.summary: FINRA reminds member firms that existing, technology‑neutral FINRA rules and securities laws fully apply when firms use generative AI (Gen AI), including large language models (LLMs), in their businesses. FINRA clarifies that the notice does not create new legal or regulatory requirements and applies whether firms build Gen AI tools in‑house or use third‑party or embedded tools. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments Relating to Protected Option and Warrant Positions Under FINRA Rule 4210
groups.summary: FINRA has amended Rule 4210 (Margin Requirements) to add a specific exception for certain "protected" short index option or warrant positions that are hedged with products tracking the same underlying index. groups.title: 2024 GASB Accounting Support Fee to Fund the Governmental Accounting Standards Board
groups.summary: FINRA announces the 2024 Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Accounting Support Fee, which is designed—under an SEC-mandated framework—to fully fund GASB’s 2024 annual budget of $18,582,100 with no offset from Financial Accounting Foundation (FAF) reserves. FINRA will collect a total of $18,582,100 from member firms that report municipal securities trades to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) by assessing $4,645,525 each calendar quarter starting in April 2024. Each member firm’s quarterly assessment is proportional to its share of the total par value of municipal securities transactions reported by all FINRA members in the prior quarter. Firms with quarterly assessments under $25 are excluded for that quarter, and their amounts are reallocated among firms with assessments of $25 or more; firms with no reportable municipal securities trades in a quarter are not charged for that period. groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Enhance Post-Trade Transparency in the U.S. Treasury Securities Market
groups.summary: FINRA, in consultation with the U.S. Department of the Treasury, has adopted amendments to enhance post-trade transparency for U.S. Treasury securities by creating two new TRACE data products focused on on-the-run nominal coupon Treasuries. Beginning March 25, 2024, FINRA will disseminate an end-of-day transaction file with capped trade sizes, providing price, size (subject to caps), counterparty type, ATS flags, and other modifiers for trades reported that day, while omitting any party-identifying information. Non-professionals can access next-day, transaction-level data for free on FINRA’s website for personal, non-commercial use, while professionals can subscribe to the end-of-day and historic data sets for specified monthly and annual fees consistent with existing TRACE pricing for other asset classes. No new reporting obligations are imposed on TRACE reporters.

groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Conform its Rules to the T+1 Settlement Cycle
groups.summary: FINRA has adopted rule amendments to align its regulatory framework with the SEC's move from a T+2 to T+1 standard settlement cycle for most broker-dealer transactions, effective May 28, 2024 (or a later SEC-designated date). groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to Improve the Accessibility of Order Routing Disclosures for NMS Securities
groups.summary: FINRA has adopted new Rule 6151 requiring member firms that are subject to SEC Rule 606(a) to submit their quarterly order routing reports for NMS securities to FINRA for centralized online publication. Introducing firms that adopt their clearing firms’ Rule 606(a) reports by reference must instead provide FINRA with a list of their clearing firms and related hyperlinks, and update this information if it changes. Reports must be submitted electronically via FINRA Gateway (manual upload) or through the fileX machine‑to‑machine interface, and firms may correct reports by submitting replacement files. FINRA will provide technical specifications and a test environment in advance and will host a centralized repository of Rule 606(a) Reports on its website, without altering firms’ existing obligations under SEC Rule 606(a).

groups.title: Amendments to the Arbitration Codes to Make Various Clarifying and Technical Changes
groups.summary: FINRA’s Regulatory Notice 24-03 announces amendments to the Codes of Arbitration Procedure for Customer and Industry Disputes, effective for cases filed on or after March 4, 2024. groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 24-02 announces the effective dates and core operational requirements of two new supervisory rule supplements—FINRA Rule 3110.19 (Residential Supervisory Location) and FINRA Rule 3110.18 (Remote Inspections Pilot Program)—and sets the end date for COVID-19-related relief on updating office information on Forms U4 and BR. groups.title: Final Statements for Broker-Dealers, Investment Adviser Firms, Agents and Investment Adviser Representatives, and Branches
groups.summary: FINRA’s Regulatory Notice 24-01 explains the 2024 Final Statements process for broker-dealers and investment advisers participating in the Renewal Program. Final Statements, available in E-Bill as of January 2, 2024, reconcile renewal fees for BD and IA registrations and notice filings based on year-end status in CRD and IARD. Overpayments from Preliminary Statements were transferred to firms’ Flex-Funding Accounts on January 2, 2024; firms may request refunds via E-Bill or retain the credit for future use, with refund checks resuming January 29, 2024. If the Final Statement shows additional amounts due versus the Preliminary Statement, firms must remit payment and report any discrepancies to FINRA by January 26, 2024. groups.title: FINRA Reminds Member Firms of Net Capital, Recordkeeping and Financial Reporting Requirements in Connection with Revenue Recognition Practices
groups.summary: FINRA alerts member firms that misapplication of ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers) in recognizing fees from customer contracts has led to violations of SEA Rules 15c3-1 (Net Capital), 17a-3 (Recordkeeping), and 17a-5 (Financial Reporting). Examinations found firms prematurely recognizing non-refundable M&A fees as revenue without performing or documenting the ASC 606-required performance obligation analysis, causing overstated revenues, understated liabilities and non-allowable assets, and in some cases net capital deficiencies or material reductions in excess net capital. FINRA instructs firms to adopt and consistently apply documented ASC 606-compliant revenue recognition policies; analyze each contract to identify performance obligations and when they are satisfied; maintain required books and records; and ensure FOCUS reports, Supplemental Statement of Income filings, and annual reports (including ASC 606 footnote disclosures) are all prepared in conformity with ASC 606 and SEA Rule 17a-5.

groups.title: FINRA Highlights Available Guidance and Resources Related to Regulation Best Interest
groups.summary: FINRA Regulatory Notice 23-20 highlights existing SEC and FINRA guidance and tools to help broker-dealers comply with Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI) without creating new legal obligations. The Notice summarizes SEC Reg BI requirements, emphasizing the four component obligations (Care, Disclosure, Conflict of Interest, and Compliance) and the relationship between Reg BI and the Investment Advisers Act fiduciary standard. It directs members to SEC staff Bulletins on account recommendations, conflicts of interest, and care obligations, which provide Q&A-style interpretive guidance on topics such as reasonably available alternatives, retirement rollovers, documentation practices, conflicts arising from product menus and compensation, and recommendations of complex or risky products. groups.title: FINRA Discontinues Collection of INSITE Data From Clearing Firms
groups.summary: FINRA announces that, effective November 30, 2023, it will discontinue collecting data from clearing and self-clearing firms under Rule 4540, which historically supported the Integrated National Surveillance and Information Technology Enhancements (INSITE) program. The decision is driven by the availability of alternative data sources—such as CAT data, supplemental FOCUS reports under Rule 4524, and margin statistics under Rule 4521(d)—that either replicate or improve upon the information previously gathered, enabling more granular risk assessment. FINRA intends this change to reduce reporting burdens and costs for clearing firms without weakening regulatory oversight. FINRA will update its website to reflect the elimination of all Rule 4540 data elements, and notes that if future regulatory needs require renewed data collection under Rule 4540, it will provide advance notice via a Regulatory Notice or similar communication.

groups.title: FINRA Adopts TAF Exemption for Proprietary Trading Firms
groups.summary: FINRA has amended its By-Laws to exempt proprietary trading firms from paying the Trading Activity Fee (TAF) on transactions executed on national securities exchanges where they hold membership. This change, effective November 6, 2023, is designed to align with recent SEC amendments to Exchange Act Rule 15b9-1, which will require many proprietary trading firms to become FINRA members if they conduct trading off of their member exchanges. Under the new TAF exemption, a proprietary trading firm must (i) trade only its own capital, (ii) have no customers other than brokers or dealers (including a six‑month lookback), and (iii) conduct all trading through firm or affiliate accounts by owners, employees, or contractors. Trades executed off a member exchange, or on exchanges where the firm is not a member, remain subject to TAF unless another exemption applies. Both newly joining and existing FINRA member proprietary trading firms that meet these conditions are eligible for the exemption.

groups.title: FINRA Amends Its Rules to Allow Video Conference Hearings Before the Office of Hearing Officers and the National Adjudicatory Council Under Specified Conditions

groups.title: FINRA Seeks Comment on Concept Proposal for a Liquidity Risk Management Rule

groups.title: FINRA Reminds Members of Their Obligations When Selling Private Placements

groups.title: FINRA Adopts Amendments to FINRA Rule 8312 to Release Information on BrokerCheck Relating to Designation as a Restricted Firm
